raw_response:
I’m 66 this year, and I’ve farmed here in Quzhou my whole life, so I don’t like making big changes unless I have a reason. With only 2 people in the house and some off-farm work, I have to keep the work manageable and the cash use steady. Wheat-maize is still my backbone because it is the safest way to keep grain and income on the same land. Cotton and stevia I keep on smaller pieces. Cotton can still bring cash if I manage it carefully, and stevia gives me another line of income, but I won’t put too much land into crops that need more watching. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I’ll save irrigation for the key growth stages rather than watering too often.

For wheat, I’ll stay close to what has worked in recent years: a normal October sowing, base fertilizer first and one topdress at jointing, with 3 irrigations if the spring is dry. For maize after wheat, the turnaround is tight, so I’ll harvest wheat and plant maize right away with simple rotary tillage or direct seeding if I can get it done fast. I’ll keep cotton on a small area because it takes more labor for pest watching and picking, and at my age I can’t expand it much. Stevia I’ll plant on the smallest block and manage it a bit more carefully on fertilizer and water because that crop reacts to field condition, but I still won’t spend too aggressively. I’d rather aim for a stable year than chase the highest yield and risk spending too much.
